caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
raw_response:
The chart represents the distribution of samples based on two measures of ambiguity: standard deviation (outer ring) and maximum ambiguity (inner ring). There are six distinct slices representing different combinations of these ambiguity values. The outer ring contains a slice labeled “Std: 0.0” colored dark blue, representing approximately 49.0% of the data; a slice labeled “Std: 0.47” colored light blue, representing approximately 38.0%; a slice labeled “Std: 0.82” colored teal, representing approximately 7.0%; and a slice labeled “Std: 0.94” colored purple, representing approximately 5.0%. The inner ring contains a slice labeled “Max: 1” colored pink, representing approximately 39.0%; a slice labeled “Max: 2” colored cyan, representing approximately 47.7%; and a slice labeled “Max: 3” colored light gray, representing approximately 14.2%. A white ring is present between the two rings. The chart includes percentage labels within each slice, and the segments appear ordered from largest to smallest, with the largest slice being “Max: 2”.
